notes: PRJEB39943 is the 2019 CCRE survey (36-37 countries, ~6-month collection). ENA holds 2904 K. pneumoniae and 530 E. coli (total 3434). The paper is a Greek national follow-up study that draws on only 128 CCRE isolates from 15 Greek hospitals (4.4% coverage of deposited K. pneumoniae). Sizing pattern B: paper covers a single-country subset of a large multi-country deposit. Study-level attributes graded from EBI description which explicitly covers the whole project. amr_study=mixed because EBI description states 'Both resistant and comparator susceptible isolates were collected' — this is a deliberate two-category contrast (resistant cases + susceptible comparators). amr_target=carbapenem because carbapenem resistance is the primary and dominant selection target (colistin is secondary/conjunctive in 'and/or colistin'); the survey and all analyses are framed around carbapenem resistance. amr_method=ast_result because the CCRE protocol classifies isolates by phenotypic R/I/S categories per EUCAST breakpoints (confirmed in paper for Greek arm; same protocol applied across all 37 countries). No single country backfill possible (37 countries). Isolation source is diverse clinical specimens (infection and carriage across multiple specimen types); no single predominant value determinable. Host=human applies project-wide (hospital patients across all 37 countries). Collection year 2019 for the CCRE component; specific months of the six-month window not stated in available text.

notes: SIZING: ENA holds 1820 Klebsiella samples but the paper describes only 328 K. pneumoniae isolates (~18% coverage) — Pattern C (shared/umbrella accession). Notably, 1554 ENA samples are taxon-labelled 'Klebsiella pneumoniae 11227-1', a strain-level designation absent from the paper, likely representing a large additional deposit unrelated to the described 8-year study. The EBI study title/description explicitly describes an MDR K. pneumoniae hospital outbreak study in Saudi Arabia and was used as the basis for gradeable study-level attributes (study_setting, amr_study, amr_target). AMR SELECTION: All isolates required MDR K. pneumoniae status (resistance ≥3 drug classes) to enter the cohort, established by AST as the primary method (MDR phenotype) supplemented by PCR for β-lactamase genes; amr_target is 'other' because selection was for broad MDR (multiple classes), not specifically 3GC or carbapenem. amr_method graded partial because 18% paper coverage falls below 75% and EBI description does not specify the determination method. COHORT AGE: graded partial/mixed because the age range 11–75 is stated only for the ST2096 subgroup (n=120 patients); the 11-year minimum straddles the newborn_young_child boundary. ISOLATION SOURCE: specimens span blood (124), urine (59), and wounds/sputum (140); no single source exceeds ~95%, so applies_whole_project false; blood culture proposed as the largest specific single category. PAPER/EBI MISMATCH: EBI title references an outbreak ending March 2018; the paper provided extends the study to September 2022, indicating the paper is a later/extended version of the original submission.

notes: The paper retrieved is entirely wrong for this accession — it describes Salmonella enterica from Malawi water environments and has no connection to PRJEB37378. A manual search for the actual DRUM study publication is needed. All study-level grading is therefore based exclusively on the EBI study title and description. DRUM is a community-based One Health study recruiting 400 households across Malawi and Uganda, selecting specifically for ESBL-producing K. pneumoniae (and E. coli) from human stool, animal stool, and environmental samples — making this amr with a third_gen_cephalosporin target. amr_method is graded partial/ast_result because 'ESBL' is a phenotypic designation most naturally detected by selective chromogenic agar (phenotypic AST-based method), but the EBI description does not explicitly name the selection method. Backfill for country cannot be assigned (two countries: Malawi and Uganda, no counts to determine 95%+ predominance); isolation_source and host cannot be assigned (multiple types: human stool, animal stool, and environmental). Cohort_age is not_gradeable because the study spans human subjects of unspecified age plus animal and environmental samples. No collection dates are mentioned in the EBI metadata.

study_setting.evidence_quote: collected in 2019 and 2020 from 175 hospitals based on antimicrobial susceptibility testing results in each hospital across Japan (covering 45 out of 47 prefectures)

amr_study.evidence_quote: E. coli and K. pneumoniae isolates resistant to 3GCs (either cefotaxime (CTX), ceftazidime (CAZ), ceftriaxone (CTRX), or cefpodoxime (CPDX)) and Enterobacterales isolates with reduced susceptibility to meropenem (MEPM) showing MIC ≥ 0.25 µg/mL... were collected

amr_target.evidence_quote: E. coli and K. pneumoniae isolates resistant to 3GCs... and Enterobacterales isolates with reduced susceptibility to meropenem (MEPM) showing MIC ≥ 0.25 µg/mL (i.e., the epidemiological cutoff defined in EUCAST for screening of carbapenemase) were collected

amr_method.evidence_quote: Paired-end sequencing (2×150 bp) was performed on the Illumina HiSeq X FIVE platform (Macrogen Japan Corporation, Tokyo, Japan) for 5,143 isolates that were selected based on the PCR results to include isolates that 1) were carbapenemase gene-positive, 2) were carbapenemase gene-negative with reduced susceptibility to carbapenems according to antimicrobial susceptibility testing results, 3) were representative in terms of ESBL gene carriage patterns; 4) did not grow in CHROMagar ESBL culture

coverage_basis: The paper describes all 5143 sequenced isolates (matching ENA total of 5144), covering the full project; ENA reports 1482 Klebsiella samples across all Klebsiella species in this accession. The paper explicitly mentions 1240 K. pneumoniae at MLST level; the remaining Klebsiella (e.g., K. aerogenes 184, K. oxytoca 19, K. variicola 46, etc.) are also covered as part of the 5143 total. Paper coverage of the full project is essentially 100%.

country.evidence_quote: collected in 2019 and 2020 from 175 hospitals based on antimicrobial susceptibility testing results in each hospital across Japan (covering 45 out of 47 prefectures)

In contrast, among the K. pneumoniae strains, the two major STs were ST12 and ST15, and the two major specimen sources were sputum and stool.

notes: Sizing: ENA PRJEB28400 holds 745 K. pneumoniae / 1950 total; the paper describes 1316 K. pneumoniae / 3153 total and cites PRJEB29424 as the deposited accession — Pattern B (paper count > ENA count). PRJEB28400 is a pre-publication subset of the full study; its EBI description confirms 'pre-publication release.' The paper fully describes the study design governing all samples in this accession. AMR study: all sequenced isolates were recovered exclusively on selective media for ESBL producers and carbapenem-resistant organisms — every isolate had to pass an AMR phenotypic gate → amr. AMR target is 'other' because the selection criterion was compound (ESBL/3GC OR carbapenem resistance), not exclusively one category. AMR method is ast_result (selective chromogenic/inhibitory media plus Vitek-2 AST). Cohort: inclusion criterion explicitly states 'all adult patients'; age table shows a small 0–20 group which represents 18–20-year-olds meeting the adult criterion → cohort_age = adult, gradeable. Isolation source for K. pneumoniae is genuinely mixed (62.5% stool, 24.7% sputum, 4.8% urine, 6.5% environmental, 1.3% skin swab); no single source reaches ~95%, so applies_whole_project = false; plurality proposed_value = stool for curator reference. Host: ~93.5% of K. pneumoniae isolates are clinical (from human patients), with 6.5% environmental (hospital surfaces/equipment); environmental minority is small enough to apply 'human' project-wide per the rubric's small-minority exception.

study_setting.evidence_quote: We collected all isolates from clinical samples sent to these hospitals' clinical microbiology laboratories that, using the laboratories' standard operating procedures, were identified as Enterobacterales with a meropenem minimum inhibitory concentration (MIC) ≥ 2 μg/mL.

amr_study.evidence_quote: For each resistant isolate, we also collected date- and species-matched meropenem-susceptible isolates. UCI submitted two carbapenem-susceptible isolates per resistant isolate; the other three hospitals submitted a single susceptible isolate per resistant isolate. In total, we collected 347 new isolates (147 resistant and 200 susceptible isolates; one isolate per patient).

amr_target.evidence_quote: identified as Enterobacterales with a meropenem minimum inhibitory concentration (MIC) ≥ 2 μg/mL, the threshold that we used to define resistance throughout our analysis. We thus included samples categorized as both intermediate (2 μg/mL) and resistant (≥ 4 μg/mL) by the Clinical and Laboratory Standards Institute interpretative criteria.

amr_method.evidence_quote: identified as Enterobacterales with a meropenem minimum inhibitory concentration (MIC) ≥ 2 μg/mL, the threshold that we used to define resistance throughout our analysis.

coverage_basis: The paper covers all 608 isolates deposited under PRJNA271899 (261 previously sequenced + 347 newly collected). K. pneumoniae accounted for 52% of 608 isolates (~316), but the total Klebsiella count (including K. oxytoca, K. aerogenes, etc.) is not stated explicitly. ENA reports 730 Klebsiella samples out of 1219 total; the ~2× multiplier vs the paper's 608 isolates is explained by dual library submissions (short paired-end + long-insert mate-pair per isolate). Coverage of the ENA Klebsiella set is effectively 100%.

notes: SIZING: ENA accession PRJEB30134 holds 760 total samples (201 Klebsiella), substantially more than the paper's 165 carbapenemase-producing isolates (~60 Klebsiella). Paper coverage is ~30% of ENA Klebsiella — below the 75% threshold. This is a scenario-B pattern: the ENA accession is an umbrella of broader MDRO surveillance at Addenbrooke's (CUH) described in the EBI study description ('~100 isolates/month over one year' covering E. coli, Klebsiella, Staphylococci), while the paper analyses only the carbapenemase-producing subset collected over 6 years. STUDY_SETTING: Graded hospital/gradeable from EBI title ('at Addenbrooke_s_hospital') and paper confirming hospital inpatient dominance (>93% hospital-onset or healthcare-associated); 9/165 GP-referred community samples in the paper's subset are a small minority not mentioned in the EBI-level description, and paper coverage is insufficient to override the EBI whole-project framing. AMR_STUDY/TARGET/METHOD: Graded partial because paper coverage <75%; the paper's subset is clearly amr (carbapenemase selection via AST/selective media), but the broader 760-sample ENA collection may encompass other MDRO categories not described by this paper. amr_method = ast_result because primary selection used phenotypic AST or carbapenem-selective culture media; allele-level PCR was used afterwards for characterisation, not for selection. COHORT_AGE: Paper shows age range 0–95; mixed is clear for the paper's subset but cannot be applied whole-project due to <75% coverage. ISOLATION_SOURCE: Rectal swab predominates (71%) in the paper's subset but does not reach the ~95% threshold for whole-project application; source distribution for the broader 760-sample collection (including Staphylococci and other organisms) is unknown. MALDI-TOF MS identified 128 K. pneumoniae (82.6 %), 18 Klebsiella variicola (11.6 %), 7 Klebsiella oxytoca (4.5 %) and 2 Klebsiella aerogenes (1.3 %) isolates among these. The remaining 87 Thai isolates analyzed in the paper come from a prior deposit (Leangapichart et al.) and are not in this accession.

All study-level attributes apply consistently across all 9 accessions (same national surveillance design, same AMR gate, same country and setting). amr_study = amr: the inclusion criterion is confirmed carbapenemase-producer status, which is an explicit AMR gate at the reference-laboratory level (consistent with rubric: 'reference-centre collections selected by resistance-gene positivity'). amr_method = pcr_gene_presence: 'confirmed as carbapenemase-producer' at a national reference laboratory (National CPE Reference Laboratory, Galway University Hospital) implies molecular identification of a specific carbapenemase gene (OXA-48, NDM, KPC, VIM etc.); phenotypic detection alone cannot reliably identify OXA-48 producers (63.4% of the collection), so definitive confirmation at this level requires molecular methods.
